title: The Monsoon of the Coral Triangle
premise: Theo Zhou, a riverboat captain hiding from her family's treasonous past, salvages a chest bearing the seal of a nation that no longer exists — and finds inside a map to her mother's last secret. Hunted by the collector who financed her debt and shadowed by an archivist who claims to be her half-brother, she assembles a ragged crew and races across the mountains ahead of the snows, when glacier calving opens the pass for only days. At the frozen archive beyond the ice, Theo must choose between destroying the evidence that would clear her family's name at the cost of her crew's lives, or surrendering the truth. She chooses truth, loses the chest, and gains something rarer: a family that chose her back.
about_author: Noor Thornbury is a former marine cartographer who spent six years charting tidal rivers across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. Her novels blend nautical precision with restless, wind-driven prose about people who live between borders.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Receipts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Running cargo on the Serei Delta, Theo nets a sealed chest stamped with the extinct Republic of Vhalen's crest instead of her usual smuggled goods. The emotional beat is wary curiosity: she recognizes the seal, and it terrifies her, because her mother once served that dead government. Ends with the collector Maraval's men arriving at the dock asking questions.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Salt
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Maraval reveals he holds Theo's boat mortgage and offers forgiveness for the chest. She refuses, sensing his interest isn't archival but political. Emotional beat: pride over prudence as she burns her mooring papers and goes river-nomad. Introduces deckhand Bao and cook Imara, the first threads of her found family tightening around her.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Shares Her Eyes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Jun Zhou, who boards under pretense of cataloguing salvage and reveals he believes he's Theo's half-brother, carrying their mother's letters. Theo doesn't trust him; the letters are too accurate. Emotional beat: grief weaponized — he knows things about her childhood no stranger should. She lets him stay aboard, watching him constantly.

chapters.title: What the Chest Would Not Open
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. The chest resists every key until Imara notices the lock reads tide-tables, not tumblers. Inside: a glacial route map to the Vhalen Ice Archive and a confession naming Theo's mother a traitor — or a hero, depending on which account survives. Emotional beat: the crew debates loyalty vs. truth around the galley table while Maraval's gunboat shadows them upstream.

chapters.title: Rapids, Reckonings
chapters.summary: Bao's POV. A night run through the Kessing Rapids to lose the gunboat nearly drowns Bao; Theo dives after him against all sense. Emotional beat: Bao realizes Theo would die for her crew but not for herself, and the crew quietly decides she's theirs now, whether she consents or not. The gunboat breaks its hull; Maraval continues overland.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. The crew abandons the boat and begins the mountain crossing, racing the calving season that briefly opens the glacier route. Jun confesses he was sent by Maraval originally but has turned. Emotional beat: Theo tests his claim by giving him the worst rope on the climb — and he doesn't complain. Trust begins, grudgingly, like thaw.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The glacier calves early, splitting the route and stranding Imara on the far side of a crevasse field. The rescue costs them two days and most of their supplies. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into ferocity — Theo understands she is no longer invisible because these people refuse to let her be. Behind them, Maraval's party gains ground on the moraine.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. They reach the Vhalen Ice Archive: a vault of records proving Theo's mother exposed a massacre, not committed one. Maraval arrives with armed men, offering the crew safe passage in exchange for the documents' destruction. Emotional beat: each crew member, offered individually, refuses — the found family holds under pressure it was never built for.

chapters.title: Truth Is a Heavy Cargo
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Maraval fires the archive; the crew saves what they can carry, and Theo chooses to broadcast the surviving pages via the expedition's emergency beacon rather than flee with them. Maraval falls into the calving fissure pursuing the master ledger. Emotional beat: victory that feels like loss — the truth is free, but so is everything they suffered to carry it.

chapters.title: Where the Water Goes After
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue tone. Spring melt carries them back downriver on a borrowed barge, name-cleared and penniless. Jun stays; Bao and Imara sign onto a new boat Theo buys with the reward for Maraval's recovered ledgers. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — she names the boat after her mother, and for the first time, the river feels like a homecoming instead of an escape.
